boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Wilderness record (May 5-7, 1864) in Grant's Overland Campaign [May-June 1864]. Spotsylvania Court House (VA048) begins on May 8. Campaign-wide marches, captures, returns, reinforcements and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen and live force fields read 162,920 (US 101,895; CS 61,025). Humphreys gives the Army of the Potomac 99,438 officers and men 'present for duty equipped' on the April 30 morning report, and the Ninth Corps, reported separately, 923 officers and 18,408 enlisted men present for duty on its April return, adding that all but 6,000 of its enlisted men had just entered the service. For Lee's army he uses the April 20 return (Third Corps 1,551 officers and 20,648 men; cavalry 467 and 7,932), Longstreet's two divisions' March 31 return and Taylor's estimate of 10,000, and reconstructs a May 1 total of not less than 61,953 officers and men.
claims.rationale: Returns of different dates (March 31, April 20 and 30) and scopes; Humphreys' Confederate total is his reconstruction from mixed returns and an estimate, and his Union figures separate the Ninth Corps. None is adopted as a matched opening strength; live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: Meade says it had been determined to turn the enemy's right flank to avoid the Mine Run intrenchments. Humphreys says Lee told Ewell it was preferred not to bring on a general engagement before Longstreet came up, that Grant did not intend or wish to fight in the Wilderness, and that on May 7 Grant decided to continue by the left flank toward a general engagement in more open country.
claims.rationale: Stated aims from an interested report and history; Humphreys argues against Badeau's reading of Grant's intent.

claims.value: Humphreys says Meade, on learning of Ewell's approach, directed Warren to halt and attack with his whole force, and that Grant and Meade remained on a knoll near Wilderness Tavern during the battle. Meade writes that the lieutenant-general directed the movement and advised him that Burnside's Ninth Corps was ordered up. The frozen commanders are Lieutenant General Grant and Major General Meade (US) and General Lee (CS); the live page lists Grant and 'Major General Robert Lee' and omits Meade.
claims.rationale: Direction is attributed as the sources state; the live rank for Lee is not adopted. No listed commander receives automatic sole credit.

claims.value: The frozen result reads Inconclusive (Grant continued his offensive); the live result reads Indecisive and NPS calls the battle a tactical draw. Meade says the fighting of May 6 substantially ended the battle, the enemy having withdrawn from Hancock's front on May 7 into a strong intrenched line; NPS says the Federals advanced by the left flank toward Spotsylvania on May 7.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 29,800 (US 18,400; CS 11,400); the live field reads 28,800 (US 18,000; CS 10,800). Humphreys, combining regimental killed and missing with the medical director's wounded and Burnside's report, gives the Army of the Potomac and Ninth Corps 2,265 killed, 10,220 wounded and 2,902 missing (15,387), and estimates that 200 wounded perished in the fires. He gives the Medical and Surgical History's Confederate figures of 2,000 killed, 6,000 wounded and 3,400 missing, noting that their authority is not given, and Ewell's report of 1,250 killed and wounded in his corps.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Humphreys' Union total is his own combination of differently sourced components.

open_questions: Grant's report (No. 1), Lee's reports (No. 273), the corps and division reports, the compiled casualty returns, Meade's casualty inclosure (garbled in OCR) and Humphreys' Appendices A–C remain deferred. The middle of Humphreys' Chapter II (pp.26–52, May 5–6 fighting) was not read.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Humphreys' The Virginia Campaign of ’64 and ’65 (1883) is an interested history by the Army of the Potomac's chief of staff, in the same author family as the registered From Gettysburg to the Rapidan, and it shares headquarters papers with Meade's and Sheridan's reports. Meade's, Sheridan's, Hampton's, Butler's and Wild's reports, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XXXVI, Parts 1 and 2, are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
